hints.title: Prefix Xor Invariance
hints.text: A subarray nums[j..i] has xor sum X if and only if pref[i] ^ pref[j - 1] == X, which means pref[j - 1] == pref[i] ^ X.

hints.title: Two Alternating States
hints.text: Maintain dp1[P] (ways ending with a segment of xor x1 having prefix xor P) and dp2[P] (ending with xor x2).

hints.title: Transition via Prefix Map
hints.text: For current prefix P, ways to end with x1 comes from previous partitions ending with x2 with prefix P ^ x1, and vice-versa.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
from collections import defaultdict

class Solution:
    def countAlternatingXorPartitions(self, nums: list[int], x1: int, x2: int) -> int:
        MOD = 1_000_000_007
        dp1_map = defaultdict(int)
        dp2_map = defaultdict(int)
        
        dp2_map[0] = 1
        dp1_map[0] = 1
        
        pref = 0
        cur_ways1 = cur_ways2 = 0
        for x in nums:
            pref ^= x
            cur_ways1 = dp2_map[pref ^ x1] % MOD
            cur_ways2 = dp1_map[pref ^ x2] % MOD
            
            dp1_map[pref] = (dp1_map[pref] + cur_ways1) % MOD
            dp2_map[pref] = (dp2_map[pref] + cur_ways2) % MOD
        
        if x1 == x2:
            return cur_ways1
        return (cur_ways1 + cur_ways2) % MOD
```

complexity.notes: Single pass with hash map state lookups.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Checking all 2^(n-1) partition splits is exponential.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Prefix XOR frequency maps take O(n) space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Expects prefix XOR identity combined with two-state alternating DP.
